(a) Authority.—Subsection (a) of section 1202 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (Public Law 109–163; 119 Stat. 3455–3456) is amended—
        (1) in the heading, by striking “Fiscal Years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “Fiscal Years 2008 and 2009”; and 
        (2) in the matter preceding paragraph (1)—
            (A) by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”; and 
            (B) by striking “$500,000,000” and inserting “$977,441,000”.   
    (b) Quarterly Reports.—Subsection (b) of such section is amended by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”.

fable.w: The section only extends the fiscal years and raises the dollar cap of an existing defense authority, and updates the years for a quarterly reporting requirement. The tempting reading is that "Quarterly Reports" signals a participatory process, but such reports go to Congress, which is inside the federal government. Nothing in the text brings states, the public, experts, or any other outside party into a federal decision.
fable.s: (b) Quarterly Reports.—Subsection (b) of such section is amended by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”.

qwen_block.w: This section merely updates fiscal years and funding amounts for a federal program and requires quarterly reports. It does not involve consultation with or participation by any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). Reports to Congress or internal agency reporting are considered internal government actions, not participation.
qwen_block.s: (b) Quarterly Reports.—Subsection (b) of such section is amended by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”.
qwen_block.b:
1. **Think briefly**: The section amends a statute to update fiscal years and funding amounts for a program and requires "Quarterly Reports." The tempting reading is that "Quarterly Reports" implies some form of oversight or participation. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress or internal government reporting are "No" because Congress and federal agencies are inside the government. There is no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory boards with outside members, or consultation with states/tribes/public. The text is purely administrative/amending internal federal authority and reporting requirements.

qwen_chat.s: (a) Authority.—Subsection (a) of section 1202 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (Public Law 109–163; 119 Stat. 3455–3456) is amended— (1) in the heading, by striking “Fiscal Years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “Fiscal Years 2008 and 2009”; and (2) in the matter preceding paragraph (1)— (A) by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”; and (B) by striking “$500,000,000” and inserting “$977,441,000”. (b) Quarterly Reports.—Subsection (b) of such section is amended by striking “fiscal years 2006 and 2007” and inserting “fiscal years 2008 and 2009”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "Quarterly Reports" implies some form of public disclosure or participation. However, the text only amends the fiscal years for which reports are required; it does not specify who receives the reports or if they are public. Even if they were public, reporting is generally distinct from the interactive "consultation" or "coordination" defined as participation, unless it involves a comment period or hearing. More importantly, the primary action here is amending appropriation amounts and reporting timelines, which are internal administrative or legislative compliance tasks. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or outside experts before making a decision. The actors involved are the federal government (amending its own laws) and potentially Congress (receiving reports).
